findings.evidenceJa: 贅を尽くして造られた空間
findings.governingReading: The lavishly constructed space is destroyed around Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes one designed space into multiple rooms.

findings.evidenceJa: 本来実像を持たぬ影
findings.governingReading: The shadow by nature has no real image or material form.
findings.explanation: The English says it used to be shapeless, implying it now possesses an ordinary shape rather than borrowing manifestation through Sakura.

findings.highlight: having a physical form is torture
findings.evidenceJa: この世界に肉を持って存在する事自体が拷問
findings.governingReading: For Sakura as she merges with the shadow, existing with flesh in this world is itself torture.
findings.explanation: The English removes this-world incompatibility and reduces the torment to embodiment in general.

findings.evidenceJa: 大気はすでに猛毒
findings.governingReading: The ordinary atmosphere is already a deadly or virulent poison to what Sakura is becoming.
findings.explanation: The English removes the poison’s extreme lethality.

findings.evidenceJa: 自己を忘れ、正気を失い
findings.governingReading: Sakura forgets herself and loses sanity as she lashes out.
findings.explanation: The English preserves lost sanity but removes loss of self, a central stage of her transformation.

findings.evidenceJa: 無関心な外界に、無理解な世界に
findings.governingReading: Sakura appeals to an indifferent outside world and a world that does not understand her.
findings.explanation: The English collapses two distinct relations into one unconcerned world and omits incomprehension.

findings.evidenceJa: 肉の器
findings.governingReading: Zouken expects Sakura to turn into a vessel of flesh.
findings.explanation: The English removes flesh, weakening the bodily-transfer mechanism of his plan.

findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントを抱え込めば込むほど
findings.governingReading: The more Servants Sakura keeps held within herself, the more power she draws.
findings.explanation: The English turns containment and captivity into deliberate control, strengthening her agency.

findings.highlight: the Holy Grail receives from the Great Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 大聖杯から魔力を受信する小聖杯
findings.governingReading: The Lesser Grail receives magical energy from the Greater Grail.
findings.explanation: The English drops the Lesser Grail term and uses generic Holy Grail, weakening the two-part system.

findings.evidenceJa: 敵意を持つ者、殺意を持つ者
findings.governingReading: Sakura reacts to those bearing hostility and those bearing killing intent.
findings.explanation: The English collapses both triggers into hostility and removes the specifically lethal category.

findings.highlight: she will not obey his command
findings.evidenceJa: 言いつけを聞くようになるとは思えない
findings.governingReading: Assassin sees no reason to think loss of sanity will make Sakura meekly obey Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English promotes his skeptical prediction into certainty and removes the abject-obedience nuance.

findings.highlight: cannot approach merely by hiding your hostility
findings.evidenceJa: 殺気を消す程度では近寄れぬ
findings.governingReading: Even erasing one’s killing intent would not permit approach.
findings.explanation: The English again softens killing intent to hostility and changes erasure into concealment.

findings.highlight: She’s begging me for help now
findings.evidenceJa: 助けてくださいお爺さま
findings.governingReading: Zouken claims Sakura pleads, “Please help me, Grandfather.”
findings.explanation: The English reports begging but removes the quoted familial address central to his sadistic regression fantasy.

findings.highlight: all the days of pain and solitude over the last eleven years
findings.evidenceJa: 十一年に渡る壺毒の日々
findings.governingReading: Zouken names Sakura’s eleven years as days of kodoku, the poison-jar ordeal of organisms consuming one another.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the concrete ritual-horror image with generic pain and solitude.

findings.evidenceJa: おぬしはワシの作品
findings.governingReading: Zouken calls Sakura his work or creation.
findings.explanation: The English adds evaluative supremacy, calling her his masterpiece before the line’s grotesque promise to watch the work finish.

findings.highlight: Your mind did not follow me
findings.evidenceJa: おぬしの精神だけはついてこなかった
findings.governingReading: Only Sakura’s psyche failed to keep pace with the eleven years of bodily conditioning.
findings.explanation: The English makes Zouken the person her mind did not follow, implying disobedience rather than failed adaptation.

findings.highlight: She does not mind what we do
findings.evidenceJa: 大人しく頷きおった
findings.governingReading: Zouken claims Illya meekly nodded agreement because opening the gate fulfills her purpose.
findings.explanation: The English invents indifference to their actions and removes the observable, possibly coerced assent.

findings.highlight: I need her to keep her original form
findings.evidenceJa: 本来の姿になって貰わねばならん
findings.governingReading: Zouken needs Illya to assume or return to her proper original form.
findings.explanation: The English reverses transformation into preservation of her current form.

findings.evidenceJa: 全ての源たる心臓の地
findings.governingReading: Zouken calls the Grail site the land of the heart that is the source of everything.
findings.explanation: The English replaces heart/source imagery with an undefined “origin,” obscuring the ritual geography.

findings.evidenceJa: 昏い悦び
findings.governingReading: Dark joy at Shirou’s arrival temporarily surpasses Sakura’s pain.
findings.explanation: The English removes both emotional joy and its ominous darkness, leaving generic pleasure.

findings.evidenceJa: くすり、という笑い声
findings.governingReading: A small audible chuckle follows Sakura’s remark.
findings.explanation: The English changes sound into a silent facial expression.

findings.evidenceJa: 影を纏ったまま
findings.governingReading: Sakura leaves while still cloaked in shadow, accompanied by the black swordsman.
findings.explanation: The English preserves her companion but removes the shadow enveloping her.
